Build cell-type-resolved cross-omic network

Source: R/network-build.R
run_celltype_network.Rd

Given a SCEE with pseudobulk transcriptomics and donor-level metabolomics, constructs a block-calibrated conditional independence network for a specified cell type.

Usage

run_celltype_network(
  x,
  metabolites = NULL,
  celltype,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  exposure = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  method = c("coglasso", "block_glasso"),
  stability = TRUE,
  nlambda_w = 15L,
  nlambda_b = 15L,
  subsample_ratio = 0.8,
  rep_num = 20L,
  min_cells = 10L,
  top_var_genes = NULL,
  lambda_w = 0.3,
  lambda_b = 0.5,
  precomputed_network = NULL,
  transform = c("vst", "log_cpm"),
  genes = NULL
)

Arguments

x

SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

metabolites

Numeric matrix; rows = donors, cols = metabolites. Row names must be donor IDs. A matrix without columns, or a missing or infinite value for an analysed donor, is an error, and so is a column with the name of another column or of a gene that becomes a node: two nodes cannot have the same name. The matrix is needed to estimate a network; the default, NULL, is for a call with precomputed_network, which does not use it.

celltype

Character; which cell type to build the network for.

celltype_col

Character; column in colData identifying cell types. Default "cell_type".

exposure

Character or NULL; exposure variable to condition on (regressed out), a column of exposureData(x); another name is an error. Default NULL.

covariates

Character vector or NULL; adjustment covariates, columns of exposureData(x); another name is an error. Donors with a missing value of exposure or of a covariate are left out, with a message. Default NULL.

method

Character; "coglasso" (default) or "block_glasso". The coglasso method uses collaborative graphical lasso with block-calibrated penalties (Albanese et al. 2026) and needs the coglasso package, version 1.1.0 or later.

stability

Logical; for method = "coglasso", whether to return the edge-level selection frequencies from XStARS in stability_scores. The coglasso penalties are chosen by XStARS either way. block_glasso uses the fixed penalties lambda_w and lambda_b, performs no stability selection and ignores this argument. Default TRUE.

nlambda_w

Integer; within-omic lambda grid size. Default 15.

nlambda_b

Integer; between-omic lambda grid size. Default 15.

subsample_ratio

Numeric strictly between 0 and 1; proportion of donors drawn in each XStARS subsample, passed to coglasso::xstars() as stars_subsample_ratio. Default 0.8.

rep_num

Integer, at least 2; number of XStARS subsamples. Default 20, as in coglasso::xstars().

min_cells

Integer; minimum cells per pseudobulk sample. Default 10.

top_var_genes

Integer or NULL; restrict to top N most variable genes for dimensionality reduction. Default NULL (all genes). Recommended: 50-200.

lambda_w

Numeric; graphical-lasso penalty for pairs of features in the same omic layer, on the correlation scale, for the block_glasso method. Default 0.3.

lambda_b

Numeric; graphical-lasso penalty for pairs of features in different omic layers, on the correlation scale, for the block_glasso method. Default 0.5.

precomputed_network

Optional named list holding a pre-estimated network to wrap into a CelltypeNetworkResult without re-estimation, with elements adjacency (symmetric binary matrix, required), precision (numeric matrix, optional), stability (numeric matrix, optional), feature_names (character vector of unique, non-missing and non-empty names, optional; taken from the column names of adjacency when absent), and either block_sizes (a named vector giving the size of each omic block) or feature_blocks (a character vector labelling each feature), both optional. The block labels become the omic_layer column of the node table, so use "transcript" and "metabolite" for the summaries and plots to recognise the layers. A logical adjacency is stored as 0/1 and its diagonal is set to zero. When provided, nothing is estimated, and of the other arguments only celltype is used. x must still be a SingleCellExposomeExperiment.

transform

Character; the transform of the pseudobulk counts. "vst" (default) is the variance-stabilising transformation of DESeq2::vst(), blind to the design, and needs DESeq2 and at least 1000 genes with a mean normalised count above 5; "log_cpm" is the base-2 logarithm of the counts per million plus one. The call stops when "vst" cannot be computed; it does not switch to the other transform. One choice stays with DESeq2: when the parametric fit of the dispersion trend fails, vst() uses a local fit, and a message says so.

genes

Character vector or NULL; row names of x, the genes that become the transcript nodes of the network, in the order given. The transform is computed from all genes of x before these are taken, so the values of a gene do not depend on which genes are kept, as they would after subsetting x. When top_var_genes is smaller than their number, the most variable of these genes are kept, in the order of their variances. Networks of several cell types built with the same genes have the same transcripts, which run_comparative_network needs, unless one of the genes is constant in a cell type and is left out there (see Details). A name that is not a row name of x, or that is the name of more than one row, is an error. Default NULL (all genes).

Value

A CelltypeNetworkResult object.

Details

The workflow proceeds as follows:

  1. Pseudobulk aggregation for the specified cell type, reusing existing exposomeSC infrastructure.

  2. Transformation of the pseudobulk counts, chosen by transform: DESeq2's variance-stabilising transformation or log-CPM. The transform is recorded in metadata(result)$transform.

  3. Constant features: a transcript or metabolite that takes one value in every donor (for example a gene with no counts in the cell type) is left out, with a message that names up to five transcripts and five metabolites; all are recorded in metadata(result)$constant_features; the call stops when every transcript or every metabolite is constant. Networks of different cell types can therefore differ in their features, which run_comparative_network does not accept. For a comparison, name the genes with genes and leave a gene that is constant in one of the cell types out of genes for all of them. top_var_genes on its own selects different genes in different cell types.

  4. Adjustment: if exposure or covariates are specified, regresses them out from both transcriptomic and metabolomic matrices. The resulting network captures the exposure-adjusted conditional dependency structure.

  5. Column-binding of the transcript values and the metabolite values (the residuals of both, where something was regressed out), each column scaled to unit variance.

  6. Block-calibrated graphical lasso estimation. With coglasso: collaborative graphical lasso with separate within/between-omic penalties and XStARS stability selection. With block_glasso: the graphical lasso (glasso::glasso()) on the correlation matrix, with the fixed penalties lambda_w within and lambda_b between omic layers, the diagonal unpenalised and no stability selection; it needs the glasso package.

  7. Returns a CelltypeNetworkResult object.

References

Albanese A, Kohlen W, Behrouzi P (2026). Multi-omics network reconstruction with collaborative graphical lasso. Bioinformatics 42(7):btag477. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btag477

Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics 9(3):432–441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

Liu H, Roeder K, Wasserman L (2010). Stability approach to regularization selection (StARS) for high dimensional graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23.

Examples

donor_ids <- paste0("D", seq_len(8L))
cell_donor <- rep(donor_ids, each = 10L)
cell_ids <- paste0("cell", seq_along(cell_donor))
counts <- outer(
    seq_len(4L),
    seq_along(cell_ids),
    function(gene, cell) 2L + ((5L * gene + 3L * cell) %% 9L)
)
storage.mode(counts) <- "integer"
dimnames(counts) <- list(paste0("G", seq_len(4L)), cell_ids)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        cell_id = cell_ids,
        donor_id = cell_donor,
        cell_type = "Monocyte"
    )
)
exposure <- matrix(seq_len(8L), ncol = 1L,
    dimnames = list(donor_ids, "exposure"))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exposure, sample_col = "donor_id")
metabolites <- outer(
    seq_len(8L),
    seq_len(2L),
    function(donor, feature) (donor + feature)^2 / 10
)
dimnames(metabolites) <- list(donor_ids, c("M1", "M2"))
if (requireNamespace("glasso", quietly = TRUE)) {
    network <- run_celltype_network(
        scee,
        metabolites,
        celltype = "Monocyte",
        method = "block_glasso",
        stability = FALSE,
        min_cells = 5L,
        top_var_genes = 3L,
        transform = "log_cpm"
    )
    network
}
#> [exposomeSC] Building block_glasso network for 'Monocyte': n=8 donors, p=5 features (3 transcripts + 2 metabolites)
#> CelltypeNetworkResult for 'Monocyte'
#>   Method: block_glasso
#>   Nodes: 5 (3 transcripts, 2 metabolites)
#>   Edges: 4 (0 cross-omic)
#>   Donors: 8
